title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — thought vere≠falso and proprie≠figurate; Vir doctus equates both with personaliter
pass_a_gloss: Placeus's first move: he had paired truly with falsely and properly with figurative/improper sense. Garrigues now collapses both adverbs into 'personally / in one's own person,' and Placeus marks that shift.
pass_b_english: PLAC. I used to think "truly" was opposed to "falsely," and "properly" to "improperly" or "figuratively," and I took them that way; but the learned man now teaches me that in this place both mean the same as "personally," or "in one's own person."
source_text: PLAC. Putabam vere opponi falso, & proprie improprie sive infigurate, atque ita accipiebam; sed docet me nunc Vir doctus utrumque hoc loco idem valere quod personaliter, vel in propria persona.

choices.choice: Placeus marks Garrigues collapse into personaliter

notes: Cap. IX PLAC vere densify section 593 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 344–345 tip).
